lessons.title: First Contact
lessons.scenario: A brand-new Catalyst switch just arrived on your desk. Before making any changes, your team lead asks you to connect to it, enter privileged mode, and take a quick look around. You need to see what commands are available and find the command that lets you enter Global Configuration mode.

objectives.label: Find out how to enter Global Configuration mode

hints: '?' lists every command valid in your current mode.

lessons.title: Give It a Name
lessons.scenario: The new switch is being prepared for the branch office rack. Your company standard requires every device to have a descriptive hostname. Set the hostname to Branch-SW1 and verify the change is reflected in the active configuration.

objectives.label: Verify the configuration with show running-config

hints: hostname <name> only works from global config mode.

lessons.title: Learning From Errors
lessons.scenario: Your mentor wants you to get comfortable experimenting at the CLI. Try entering configuration mode with odd capitalization and notice IOS accepts it anyway. Then try a show command from inside configuration mode, read the error, and learn the 'do' trick to run it without leaving config mode.

objectives.label: Enter config mode using odd capitalization
Try 'show running-config' inside config mode and read the error
Use 'do show running-config' to run it without leaving config mode

hints: 'do' prefixes any privileged/user command so it runs from inside config mode.

lessons.title: Find Your Way Around
lessons.scenario: You are shadowing a senior engineer who wants you to get comfortable with the CLI hierarchy. Move from user mode up through global configuration, drop into interface configuration, then into VLAN configuration, and find your way back to privileged mode. No changes will be saved - this is pure navigation practice.

objectives.label: Return to privileged EXEC mode with 'end'

hints: 'exit' moves up one level; 'end' jumps straight back to privileged mode from anywhere in config.

lessons.title: Type Smart, Not Hard
lessons.scenario: You are getting faster with the CLI. Your mentor shows you that you do not need to type every letter: 'en' becomes 'enable', 'int g0/2' becomes 'interface g0/2', and Tab finishes a command for you. But abbreviation has a sharp edge - IOS only accepts a shortcut if it matches exactly ONE command. 'sh st' is ambiguous (standby / stackwise-virtual / startup-config / storm-control); add letters until it's unique. On the exam, know the FULL commands.

objectives.label: Use tab completion to expand a command
Type 'sh st' and observe the ambiguous command error
Type 'sh start' and see it resolve
Use 'int g0/2' shorthand to jump to interface g0/2

hints: Ambiguous abbreviations throw '% Ambiguous command' - add letters until only one command matches.

lessons.title: Read the Switch - VLANs
lessons.scenario: A colleague just finished configuring a switch for the branch office but left before documenting it. Your job is to inspect the current state and make one small change. Use show commands to read the VLAN table, then shut down the interface that is on VLAN 20.

objectives.label: See which ports belong to which VLANs
Shut down the interface on VLAN 20

hints: show vlan brief lists access VLAN assignments per port.

lessons.title: Make and Undo
lessons.scenario: Every configuration command in IOS has an undo: type the same command with 'no' in front of it. Create VLANs 10 and 20, confirm they exist with show vlan brief, then remove both with 'no vlan' and confirm the switch is back to just the default VLAN. Tip: 'no vlan' only works from the (config)# prompt, not from inside VLAN-config mode.

objectives.label: Confirm both VLANs exist with show vlan brief

hints: Exit VLAN-config mode back to global config before running 'no vlan'.

lessons.title: Read the Switch - Interfaces
lessons.scenario: The second-floor closet switch has already been cabled for several departments. Before the change window starts, inspect the switch and confirm what is active. Then bring the down interface back to an administratively up state.

objectives.label: Show the status of all interfaces
Bring interface g0/3 to Administratively Up

hints: 'no shutdown' is the undo for 'shutdown' on an interface.

lessons.title: Save Your Work
lessons.scenario: You have spent the afternoon configuring a new switch. A maintenance window tonight includes a power cycle. If you do not save your work, every change you made will disappear when the switch reboots. Save the running configuration to startup configuration and prove the save worked.

objectives.label: Verify the startup configuration now matches

hints: 'write memory' and 'copy running-config startup-config' do the same thing.

lessons.title: Test 1 - Investigate
lessons.scenario: A switch has been handed to you with several mistakes. Use show commands to audit the device, correct the hostname, create the VLANs the site requires, bring the disabled desk port back online, and save your work. No hints are provided - this is a test of what you have learned so far.

objectives.label: Audit the device with show commands

lessons.title: Leave a Note
lessons.scenario: Your company standard requires every device to display a warning banner when someone connects. Set a message-of-the-day banner that reads: 'Authorized Access Only - Branch Office'. Then verify it is saved in the active configuration.

objectives.label: Return to User EXEC mode to trigger the banner

hints: banner motd # your message # - the delimiter character must match on both ends.

lessons.title: Security First
lessons.scenario: The branch office switch is about to be moved into the server room. Before it goes live, add an enable password so that anyone who enters privileged mode must know the password. Set the enable password to CCNA and test it.

objectives.label: Configure an unencrypted enable password of CCNA
Test the password by entering privileged mode

lessons.title: Lock the Door
lessons.scenario: The branch office switch is about to be moved into the server room. Before it goes live, you need to add basic passwords. Set an enable secret, protect the console line, and test the login.

objectives.label: Set the enable secret to CCNA
Test the secret by entering privileged mode

hints: enable secret takes priority over enable password if both are set.

lessons.title: Where is the Remote
lessons.scenario: You need to allow remote access to the switch for up to 5 simultaneous sessions. Configure VTY lines 0 through 4, set a password, and require login.

objectives.label: Set password Remote123 on the VTY lines
Require login on the VTY lines

lessons.title: Who Gets In
lessons.scenario: Shared passwords are a security risk. Your security team now requires every administrator to log in with their own username and password. Create a local user account named admin with privilege level 15, then change the VTY lines to use local username authentication instead of a shared line password. Verify the configuration in the running config.

objectives.label: Create local user admin with privilege 15
Switch VTY lines to local username login

hints: 'login local' replaces 'login' + a line password with username/password auth.

lessons.title: Test 2 - Access Review Before Go-Live
lessons.scenario: The lobby switch is almost ready for production. A previous tech already set the enable password to 'netadmin' and created the local administrator account, but the physical console still has no password and remote access has not been tied to local usernames. Enter privileged mode with the enable password netadmin, then finish the access review: secure the console line, require local authentication on the VTY lines, verify the running configuration, and save the handoff.

objectives.label: Enter privileged mode with password netadmin
Secure the console line (password lobbyconsole, login)
Secure VTY lines for local login

lessons.title: Exam - Configure Your First Switch
lessons.scenario: This is your first solo assignment. A new switch just arrived for the remote office in factory-default state. Complete the entire baseline setup using the exact values below, then verify and save. No step-by-step hints are available.

objectives.label: Set the enable password and create the local user

hints: After configuring console/VTY lines you're in line-config mode - 'end' returns you to privileged mode before show/write commands.

lessons.title: Exam - SSH Into the Switch
lessons.scenario: Final challenge. So far you have configured this switch from the directly-attached console. Real administrators rarely have that luxury - they manage switches remotely over an encrypted SSH session. Right now the switch has NO management IP and its VTY lines only accept insecure Telnet. Build the complete SSH setup in the correct order, then open the PC terminal and connect.

objectives.label: Configure VLAN 1 management IP and bring it up
Set VTY lines to login local + SSH-only transport
SSH into the switch from the PC terminal

hints: RSA key generation requires hostname AND domain name to already be set, in that order.
'transport input ssh' replaces Telnet - Telnet access is removed once this is set.
